papers.title: Phase Diagram and Theoretical Calculation Guided Rational Design of Cu 6.26 Sn 5 /Sn Heterostructured Aerogel for Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesizing hydroxylamine (NH 2 OH) from nitrite (NO 2 − ) promises a green alternative to the hazardous Raschig process, yet catalyst development is trapped in a persistent selectivity–activity dilemma. Excessively strong adsorption of intermediates on the catalyst drives the over‑reduction of * NH 2 OH to ammonia, whereas overly weak adsorption depletes the interfacial reactant supply and yields to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, guided by binary phase diagrams and density functional theory calculations, we report a one‐step co‐reduction strategy for the general synthesis of 3D intermetallic/metal heterostructured aerogels with freely tunable components—bypassing the sacrificial templates required by conventional methods. The resultant aerogel comprises a porous Sn scaffold decorated with Cu 6.26 Sn 5 intermetallic nanoparticles that form stable heterointerfaces. With cyclohexanone trapping in 0.5 m Na 2 SO 4 , the Cu 10 Sn 90 heterostructured aerogel achieves a remarkable Faradaic efficiency of 79.7% and yield rate of 0.731 mmol h −1 cm −2 toward cyclohexanone oxime. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Cu 6.26 Sn 5 phase accelerates interfacial NO 2 − accumulation and mass transport, whereas the Sn scaffold serves as the dominant active center to undergo the reduction of NO 2 − and boost * NH 2 OH desorption. papers.title: Engineering High-Entropy Tetrahedrite Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S Nanocrystals via Sequential Cation Exchange as Efficient Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reactions
papers.abstract: Abstract High-entropy chalcogenides represent an emerging class of functional materials with immense potential in broad applications. To date, colloidal high-entropy nanocrystals (NCs) have predominantly been accessed via co-nucleation of precursors or simultaneous incorporation of multiple cations. While effective, these approaches lack a mechanistic understanding of NC synthesis. Here, we report the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S NCs in the tetrahedrite phase, employing a sequential, low-temperature cation-exchange strategy, starting from a Cu–Zn–Sb–S tetrahedrite template. Subsequent sequential cation exchanges preserve the crystal phase while enabling precise control over morphology. This bottom-up approach circumvents the need for high-temperature synthesis, while allowing isolation and characterization of intermediate states, providing important mechanistic insight into the evolution of high-entropy NCs. The nanocrystals served as hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts with less negative cathodic potentials. This work introduces the high-entropy tetrahedrite phase, paving the way for entropy-stabilized chalcogenides for energy conversion applications.
